approach_stated: Parking area is at the beginning of the rocks (dirt lot by an oil derrick)

evidence.fact: Getting There: beginning of the rocks and parking area are marked by an oil derrick, dirt lot and burnt boulder.
A 1/4 mile long wall with 75 to 100 feet of climbable rock; top roping recommended.

note: MP tags these routes 'Alpine' alongside Trad/TR, probably why they were filed alpine; it is a roadside single-pitch crag.

place_name: Hyperform Wall, Lone Peak Cirque, Central Wasatch, Utah (MP area 106236577)
approach_stated: Lone Peak Cirque approach: 5600'+ vertical, six-mile hike; MP suggests 3-4 days
summit_or_glacier: cirque walls ~10,800 ft with snowfields; no glacier

evidence.fact: First wall seen after the 'death slog', before rounding into the Cirque proper.
Lone Peak Cirque: 5600'+ vertical, six-mile long approach; plan on 3 or 4 days.

place_name: Horse Creek Slabs, Absaroka Range near Dubois, Wyoming (MP area 106022084)
approach_stated: Park in pull-off after crossing Horse Creek by Horse Creek campground; slabs 'very obvious' from there (no minutes stated)
summit_or_glacier: no; limestone slab of easy bolted climbs, road-accessible

evidence.fact: Drive Horse Creek road ~9 miles to campground; slabs very obvious; park in pull-off after crossing creek.
Sharp limestone slab with easy bolted climbs; good area to try your first sport lead.

note: No approach minutes stated, but parking is beside the visible slab; sport crag.

place_name: The Indian Buttress Formation, Echo Canyon, The Others, Tahquitz, California (MP area 109903961)
approach_stated: Follow Tahquitz North Talus approach to the North Gully descent, then hike four times that distance further; 'deep in the back country'
summit_or_glacier: 600 ft dome in a backcountry cirque; no glacier

evidence.fact: Indian Buttress: located deep in the back country of The Others Cirque, a 600' dome worth the approach.
The Others, Getting There: 'Mucho hiking.'

note: No minutes stated; approach is beyond Tahquitz's own approach plus four times the North Gully distance - long backcountry, so alpine.

place_name: Dog Wall, Horseshoe Piles, Lake George, Mammoth Lakes, California (MP area 106883144)
approach_stated: Horseshoe Piles 15-20 min from Lake George lot; Dog Wall a further ~200 yd / 15 min uphill
summit_or_glacier: no; short granite craglet at 9,200 ft, TR anchors by walking above

evidence.fact: Horseshoe Piles: park at Lake George lot, Crystal Lake Trail; the approach takes 15-20 minutes.
Dog Wall: about 200 yards uphill from the piles, 15 min approach uphill; short craglet.

note: Total ~30-35 min stated across two MP pages.

place_name: Black Bluff - N. Face (Right Side), Mill Creek Rd/Skyline area, Big Bear South, San Bernardino Mtns, California (MP area 107334796)
approach_stated: About 1.5 miles following cairns from Bluff Mesa Group Campground (dirt-road access), downhill to the base; no time stated

evidence.fact: Black Bluff: remote, wild crag; granite about 80 feet high, mostly crack climbs.
From Bluff Mesa Group Campground follow cairns down a gully to the crag; about 1.5 miles.

note: Distance stated, not time; easy-to-get-lost cairned approach. Aurora Borealis, Scratch and Sniff, Shooting Star not matched on MP under this wall.

place_name: The Wart (aka Lake of the Domes Dome), Medlicott Dome, Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite, California (MP area 114784820)
approach_stated: Via Drug Dome base: 0.85 miles and 1000 ft gain; no time stated
summit_or_glacier: no; single-pitch knob sport crag beside Lake of the Domes

evidence.fact: Approach by way of Drug Dome, scramble gully to Lake of the Domes: .85 miles and 1000 ft gain.
A modern knob sport crag 50 feet from an alpine lake; one of the best in Tuolumne.

note: Distance stated not minutes; short distance from the Tioga Road domes. Route Right not matched on MP.

place_name: Junior Wall, Twin Bridges, Glen Aulin Area, Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite, California (MP area 119030469)
approach_stated: About 4 miles on the Glen Aulin trail from near Lembert Dome to the Twin Bridges, then up slabs from the PCT

evidence.fact: Twin Bridges: hike the Glen Aulin trail from near Lembert Dome about 4 miles to the bridge.
Junior Wall: work your way up slabs from the Pacific Crest Trail.

note: Sport routes, but a ~4-mile approach exceeds the 1-hour crag rule (alternate Pothole Dome river approach, no distance given).

place_name: The Wave, Wild Ridge Area, Independence Pass, Colorado (MP area 115401569)
approach_stated: Wild Ridge: park at Wild Rock pullout on CO-82, hike to base of wall; takes about 30 minutes. The Wave reached by climbing The Coral below
summit_or_glacier: no; 130 ft band above a lower tier, road-accessible

evidence.fact: Wild Ridge: park as for Wild Rock on CO Hwy 82 ... to the base of the wall. This takes about 30 minutes.
The Wave is the 130 foot band above The Coral, typically approached via Coral routes.

note: Reaching The Wave requires climbing a lower-tier route first.

place_name: Instant Karma Cliff, Independence Pass, Colorado (MP area 117607094)
approach_stated: Trail north of the Independence Pass parking lot; the approach takes 50 minutes

evidence.fact: Take a trail north of Independence Pass parking lot ... to the cliff. The approach takes 50 minutes.
Instant Karma is a nice alpine crag; descent is a walk off or a two-bolt rap.

place_name: Easter Island, Alpine Lite Cliffs, Mt. Blue Sky (Evans), Colorado (MP area 110974950)
approach_stated: Park near mile marker 8 below Summit Lake; Alpine Lite ~20 min past the saddle, about 50 minutes overall
summit_or_glacier: formation has its own small summit (60 m tower); not a mountain summit; no glacier

evidence.fact: Park near mile marker 8 before Summit Lake; Alpine Lite is a 20 minute walk over the saddle (about 50 minutes overall).
Easter Island: 60m tall on the right edge, faces north-northwest.

note: Stated 50-min approach at ~12,500+ ft off the Mt Blue Sky road; crag by the rule, though high-altitude.

place_name: The Toiyabe Fitzroy, Wild Granites, Western Nevada (MP area 117113221)
approach_stated: Cairned trail from end of dirt road: 1 hour, 2100 vertical feet
summit_or_glacier: 1200 ft dome; routes descend by rappels on the back side (top-out on the dome); no glacier

evidence.fact: Follow cairns up the ridge toe to the base of the wall: 1 hour, 2100 vertical feet.
The imposing main dome with a 1200 ft east face; routes ordered from the rappels on the back side.

note: Exactly at the 60-min line with 2100 ft gain, dirt-road access, long multipitch dome topping out - borderline, owner call.

place_name: Ross Peak (north face), Bridger Range, Bozeman, Montana (MP area 107075098)
approach_stated: Expect at least 2-3 hours if hiking quickly, from the South Brackett Creek road gate
summit_or_glacier: north face of a 9000+ ft peak; climbs start near a snowfield

evidence.fact: Approach: hug the base of the mountain, drop into the bowl toward the snow field; expect at least 2-3 hours.
Sitting at a very high 9000 feet; climbers often on the north face below peak baggers.

note: Long approach; correctly alpine despite bolted routes.

place_name: Sport Wall, Lamoille Canyon, Ruby Mountains, Nevada (MP area 110562223)
approach_stated: Parking area on the right 0.8 mi from the canyon gate; Lamoille crags are a short bushwhack from the road

evidence.fact: Getting There: Parking area on the right, 0.8 miles from canyon gate.
All of the Lamoille Canyon crags are a relatively short bushwhack from the road.

note: No minutes stated; parent page says short bushwhack from the road.

place_name: Flying Buttress, Lone Peak Cirque, Central Wasatch, Utah (MP area 105739727)
approach_stated: Via Draper or Alpine route to Lone Peak Cirque (5600+ ft, six miles); pinnacle left of Lone Peak summit
summit_or_glacier: pinnacle beside Lone Peak summit; cirque with snowfields

evidence.fact: Follow the Draper or Alpine route to Lone Peak Cirque, then the next big pinnacle left of Lone Peak Summit.
Lone Peak Cirque: 5600 ft+ vertical, six-mile approach; plan 3 or 4 days.

note: Lichen It not matched on MP under this buttress.
